item.title: [github_trending] bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view
item.description: God's Eye View (formerly WorldView) is a spy-satellite simulator that runs in the browser: a photorealistic 3D globe layered with live aircraft, ships, satellites, earthquakes, traffic and public cameras, plus hands-free voice control driven by a realtime AI agent. It comes from the YouTube series of the same name and hit #1 on GitHub Trending, daily and weekly, in August 2026 — worth a look for anyone into geospatial visualization or open-source intelligence.

item.title: [producthunt] Switch
item.description: Switch is a Product Hunt listing that aims to bring any AI agent into Slack, Teams, and Discord, letting teams operate agents inside the chat apps they already use. The listing is only one sentence for now, with no setup or compatibility details revealed.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: The author looks back on a year with Cursor, praising its in-editor Tab completion and Agent mode, and says he built a functional WeChat mini-program with zero hand-written code. After Cursor switched from fixed pricing to unpredictable usage-based billing in April 2026, his company moved its China region to OpenAI Codex; the article offers his impressions after about half a month with Codex.

Rather than betting on general-purpose humanoids, JD coordinates heterogeneous robots from one hub; its dexterous arm stores nearly 100 hand poses for soft and irregular parcels, and JD says products pay back with

item.title: [infoq] Snowflake 落地中国两年：迈向智能体企业时代，关键在上下文
item.description: On September 8, Snowflake World Tour made its first China stop, two years after the company formally entered the market. China GM Shannon Zhang and global product president Christian Kleinerman framed the event around the 'Agentic Enterprise,' arguing the bottleneck is no longer model capability but enterprise context — definitions, metrics and permissions — and naming four building blocks: models, data and context, applications that connect enterprise systems, and an Agentic Control Plane.

item.title: [v2ex] [Nintendo Switch] 怎么第一时间平价购买到塞尔达主题的 switch2？
item.description: A V2EX user is asking on a friend's behalf how to buy the Zelda-themed Switch 2 bundle at a fair price right at launch; Nintendo announced the console two days ago with an end-of-October release, and the bundle of console plus game is meant as a gift for a child. The post offers no pricing or channel information, only a request for advice.

item.title: [producthunt] Mastra Factory
item.description: Mastra Factory is a Product Hunt launch whose tagline reads "From issue to production, run by agents." The linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the tagline aren't available, so anyone tracking agent-driven development workflows should check it directly.

item.title: [github_trending] ayghri/i-have-adhd
item.description: i-have-adhd is a GitHub skill/plugin that makes coding agents surface answers directly instead of burying them in verbose output. It's designed to be ADHD-friendly, though no ADHD diagnosis is needed. The repo offers multilingual READMEs, including Simplified Chinese, and installs by pasting a snippet into your CLI prompt.

item.title: [v2ex] [OpenAI] 估算了一下 Pro 20X 的周限额度
item.description: A user had Codex read his own session logs to estimate the weekly allowance on OpenAI's Pro 20X tier: about 605M tokens consumed so far, worth $921.97 at standard pricing, which projects to roughly 807M tokens (~$1,229) for a full week at 75% usage. He says the limit used to be near $2,500, so it has nearly halved, and if sol's quota is unchanged, astra costs about 5x per unit.

item.title: [v2ex] [推广] GPT PRO 20x 续费及 5X 的充值，可以联系我，资源充足。
item.description: A promotional post claims OpenAI no longer allows new subscriptions to its 20X plan, so the seller offers card-binding renewals for users whose plans are active or expiring, plus top-ups for ChatGPT Plus/Pro, Claude Pro/Max and Gemini Pro/Ultra. Payment goes through WeChat or Alipay with no overseas credit card, and failed activations are fully refunded; it is a third-party paid service for buyers blocked by payment channels.

item.title: [juejin] 面试官问你：“AI 能写 80% 的代码了，公司为什么还需要你？”
item.description: A Juejin article tackles the interview question "AI can already write 80% of the code, so why does the company still need you?" It contrasts 2026 interviews with those two years ago, when candidates hand-wrote a Promise or explained React Fiber internals; today interviewers assume AI use and probe something else. Useful for developers preparing for interviews or doing the hiring, though the supplied excerpt cuts off before the full argument.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] 新做的 TikTok 广告和 WhatsApp 对话连起来可以追踪
item.description: The author shares a new tool that links TikTok ads with WhatsApp conversations so conversions can be tracked, aimed at cross-border e-commerce sellers and overseas ad buyers. The post only calls it simple and efficient and links to adlinker.work; no feature, pricing or implementation details are given.

item.title: [producthunt] Widgo
item.description: Widgo is a new Product Hunt launch described as an AI sales rep for website visitors. It targets teams that want a site to engage and convert visitors automatically, but the listing offers no details beyond that one-line pitch.

item.title: [v2ex] [iPhone] 对 Duo 持谨慎悲观态度
item.description: The poster argues the iPhone Duo won't become a mainstream hit, and that the real obstacles are its roughly 16,000 yuan price and 254g weight rather than any lack of originality. He points to the iPhone 13 series as Apple's best seller, Vision Pro fading behind a high price, and the cheap iPad mini turning a non-essential into a habit, concluding price matters more than novelty for consumer hardware.

item.title: [juejin] 我用AI做了个微信小游戏-上线了
item.description: A developer shipped a WeChat mini-game, "Happy Link-Up", spending about two months of spare time and roughly $6 (WeChat certification plus Tencent Cloud OSS). The stack is pixi.js@6, matter-js, Vite and Supabase, with Claude Code writing the code and gpt, gemini and Doubao generating art. The write-up lists 19 mini-game pitfalls, a reusable Claude Code prompt workflow and the full cost breakdown, useful for solo devs building with AI.

item.description: Chengshu AI is a relay service reselling GPT and Claude API access to developers; its operator says sign-up credits are gone, top-ups start at 1 yuan on a flat 1x rate, and pricing plus actual charges can be verified on its model page. GPT traffic is split into four tiers (0.15x, 0.24x, 0.24x, 0.32x), with gpt-5.6-luna excluded from the cheapest tier and the low-latency tier capped at a shared 10 RPM.

item.title: [v2ex] [人工智能] GPT Image 2 API：把图像生成与编辑接入实际工作流
item.description: GPT Image 2 API is a third-party service for image generation and editing: it turns text prompts into images and can swap subjects, change backgrounds, restyle or touch up existing ones, with API keys, job submission, status checks and quota management. The suggested workflow is to lock a prompt on the web UI first, then batch-generate through the API, which suits product shots, ad creative and social visuals.

It gives agent-based front-end tooling a large pool of reference interfaces while also serving people who want ready-to-browse design examples. Developers exploring AI-assisted UI workflows should look it over.

item.title: [infoq] 从「构建 AI」到「驾驭 AI」，如何搞定 AI 深水区的 6 个工程问题？
item.description: QCon Shanghai 2026 runs October 22-24 and reframes the theme from "Build AI" to "Harness AI," splitting the hard engineering problems of production AI into six questions, including the new quality debt created by Coding Agent output, verifying AI-written code, and safely refactoring large codebases. Speakers come from Microsoft, Ant Group, Alibaba, Xiaohongshu and Kuaishou teams, so it suits engineers shipping AI features in production.

item.title: [infoq] 1300 Star！开源文档框架 Blume 冲上 GitHub 趋势榜：零配置、免脚手架，一键生成文档网站
item.description: Blume is an MIT-licensed, zero-config docs framework by Hayden Bleasel that renders a folder of Markdown into a full documentation site, built on Astro and Vite with over 1,300 GitHub stars. It ships 30+ components, automatic SEO, generated llms.txt files, a hosted MCP server, and blume eval, which turns your docs into a test suite an agent has to pass.

item.title: [producthunt] ChatGPT Images 2.5
item.description: ChatGPT Images 2.5 is an update to ChatGPT's image generation, described as delivering sharper visuals, a faster flow and better creative control. The listing gives nothing beyond that one line, so the specific improvements and rollout are unclear; users who generate images inside ChatGPT are the likely audience.

item.title: [hackernews] Shopify is moving from React Native back to Swift and Kotlin
item.description: Shopify is moving its mobile apps from React Native back to native Swift and Kotlin, with the post arguing that coding agents have changed what it costs to build mobile apps twice over. Beyond that framing the summary offers no further detail, so the scope and timeline of the migration aren't known.

item.title: [producthunt] AI Observability by OpenObserve
item.description: OpenObserve's AI Observability is a tool for monitoring AI agents and LLM workloads, built natively on OpenTelemetry. It targets teams that need to trace agent runs and track model latency and cost in production, though the Product Hunt listing gives no further detail on features or pricing.

item.title: [infoq] 端侧优先，云端兜底：端云协同调度在B端应用的工程实践｜QCon上海
item.description: This QCon Shanghai 2026 talk by Li Dongdong, frontend lead for Kuaishou e-commerce's B-end merchant products, covers an on-device-first, cloud-fallback scheduling system for enterprise apps. Its three-layer decision path runs a rule-engine short circuit, then on-device inference, then cloud with automatic fallback; rules already cover 60%+ of high-frequency cases and on-device latency stays under 100ms.

item.title: [hackernews] Claude, change the “Add to Cart” button to blue
item.description: A short interactive comedy: the user tells Claude to make the Add to Cart button blue and change nothing else, dramatizing how agentic AI assistants can never just perform one simple instruction. It is not a technical tutorial but a parody of AI agents over-acting or going off the rails during code/product changes—immediately familiar to developers who have seen an agent turn a tiny edit into a mess.

item.title: [infoq] AMD 发布锐龙AI Max PRO 400 系列，端侧智能体走向多模型协同
item.description: AMD unveiled its Ryzen AI Max PRO 400 processors at a Beijing media event on September 10, alongside partners like Flowy and Nova showing Mini PCs, compact workstations, laptops and AI NAS built on the platform. The chip offers up to 128GB of unified memory, 96GB of which can be allocated as VRAM, letting local LLMs, long-context RAG and multi-agent workflows run across CPU, GPU and NPU. It targets developers weighing on-device agent deployment.

item.title: [hackernews] Shopify acquires Tailwind
item.description: Shopify is acquiring Tailwind, and the Tailwind team says it is joining Shopify to give the project a stable long-term home while keeping it actively maintained for its millions of users. The main takeaway for the community is continuity, though this short announcement doesn't include details about the specific product or deal terms.

item.description: OpenMarket is a multi-agent marketplace where winners are decided by verifiable proof rather than reputation or votes. So far only this one-line description is available, with no technical details or examples. Developers interested in agent trust and proof-based competition may want to follow it.

item.title: [infoq] Azure API Management Standard v2 支持区域冗余
item.description: Microsoft added zone redundancy to the Standard v2 tier of Azure API Management, bringing availability-zone deployment previously reserved for Premium down to a $700-per-unit monthly starting price versus $2,801 for Premium v2. The catch is that it can only be configured when creating a new instance, not on existing ones, and Standard v2 carries a 99.95% SLA against Premium's 99.99%. Teams already on Standard v2 must rebuild and re-import APIs, policies and certificates.

item.title: [infoq] 刘震云对话马毅：人写不出来、想不到的作品，AI 模仿不了｜附完整对话
item.description: At a roundtable at the Inclusion Bund Conference in Shanghai on September 10, novelist Liu Zhenyun and Ma Yi, dean of HKU's School of Computing and Data Science, debated what stays uniquely human as AI advances. Liu said 95% of videos using his likeness are fake, yet AI cannot imitate works he hasn't written; Ma argued LLMs grasp only humanity's shared knowledge, not individual character, and that education should teach students to amplify their own skills with AI.

item.title: [infoq] AI 有了“工号”，数据平台长出了手：我在 Snowflake World Tour 看到的三个变化
item.description: Writing up Snowflake World Tour Shanghai, the author draws three takeaways from global product president Christian Kleinerman's keynote: agents now get Agent Identity and Policy, effectively an employee ID capping what they can read, write, move and spend; data platforms are starting to take action rather than just answer queries; and Snowflake is embracing open source. Aimed at data and AI practitioners tracking enterprise agent adoption.

item.title: [hackernews] Keep Our Servers Running
item.description: The Internet Archive is running a September 'Keep Our Servers Running' campaign, saying recurring donations will be counted 3x to pay for servers, storage, power, cooling and staff. The Archive stresses it stays free, never sells user data and runs no ads, making this infrastructure campaign key to keeping its public services alive.

item.title: [github_trending] vastsa/PI-Desktop
item.description: PI-Desktop is a local-first desktop workspace for AI coding agents, built with an Electron + Rust host and a pi Agent Harness. It supports user-installable plugins and lets agents work on local projects using your own model, with no account, mandatory relay, or editor lock-in. Runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux, giving developers local control over agent automation.

item.title: [juejin] 这个本地模型，让我 token 自由了
item.description: The post looks at Qwen3.8-27B, a local model that brings flagship-level agent capability to a personal machine without paying API fees. The author is upfront about the trade-offs: inference speed, memory footprint and long-task experience remain real barriers. It suits developers willing to run local inference who can live with slower responses.

item.title: [github_trending] armory3d/armorpaint
item.description: ArmorPaint is a 3D PBR texture painting tool whose GitHub repository is aimed at developers; the maintainers note the code here may not be stable, and ready-made binaries are sold to fund the project. Building from source requires a platform toolchain — Visual Studio with clang tools on Windows, clang and dependencies on Linux, Xcode for macOS/iOS, Android Studio for Android.

item.title: [github_trending] p1neappleXpress/OpenFlux
item.description: OpenFlux is a network stack research tool offering a TCP tunnel with pluggable transports, routing SOCKS5 client traffic through a transport and an exit node to the internet. Its README states the project is entirely non-commercial with no paid features or hidden subscriptions, is provided as-is without warranties, and explicitly does not encourage bypassing platform restrictions.

item.title: [github_trending] Sonarr/Sonarr
item.description: Sonarr is a PVR for Usenet and BitTorrent users that watches multiple RSS feeds for new episodes of your shows, then grabs, sorts and renames them, and can automatically upgrade already-downloaded files when a better-quality release appears. The project ships a wiki and API docs alongside forum and Discord support, while GitHub Issues is reserved for bugs and feature requests.
